terms.definition: Passive investor supplying most fund capital; liability limited to commitment.
The fund manager; earns fees and carry; invests a GP commitment.
The governing contract setting fees, waterfall, hurdle, and governance.
Capital an LP contractually agrees to provide over the fund's life.
A GP request for LPs to wire a portion of their commitment.
Cash (or stock) returned to LPs from realizations.
Total LP commitments; a common fee and carry base.
Capital actually called and deployed.
Window (commonly ~5 yrs) during which new investments are made; fees often higher and on committed capital.
Later years focused on exits and distributions; fees usually step down.
Recurring fee (often 2%) funding GP operations; performance-independent.
Post-investment-period reduction in fee rate and/or shift of base to invested cost.
Portfolio-company fees reduce the management fee LPs owe; 100% offset is now standard.
Fees a GP charges portfolio companies (~1-2% EV; % of EBITDA); subject to offset.
Reinvesting early proceeds to offset fee drag and reach full deployment; ILPA: capped, investment-period only.
GP's profit share, standard 20%.
Whether all committed or only invested capital must be returned before carry.
Carry on profit before fees and expenses; the GP-friendly basis.
Carry on profit after fees and expenses; the basis ILPA requires.
Minimum LP return before GP earns carry; standard 8% compounded in PE, 6-7% private credit, often none in VC.
Carry only on profit above the hurdle; no catch-up; GP take below stated %.
Hurdle plus catch-up; GP eventually earns its full carry % on all profit.
Tier where the GP takes an outsized share (often 100%) until the agreed split is restored on all profit.
Ordered rules splitting each distributed dollar between LP and GP.
Carry only after all fund capital plus whole-fund pref returned; LP-protective.
Carry per realized deal; GP-favorable on timing; needs clawback.
GP returns excess carry so its final take equals the contractual % of true net profit.
Carry held back to secure a future clawback.
GP's own capital in the fund (~1-2% rule of thumb), the "skin in the game."
Early negative net returns from fees and early markdowns before exits turn returns positive.
Net asset value; the residual value of unrealized holdings.
Distributions to paid-in capital; the realized multiple of cash returned.
Residual value to paid-in capital; the unrealized (paper) multiple.
Total value to paid-in capital; the total multiple (DPI + RVPI).
Multiple on invested capital (deal level).
Money-weighted internal rate of return; timing-sensitive.
Public Market Equivalent; benchmarks PE cash flows against a public index.
Kaplan-Schoar PME; a ratio, above 1 means PE beat the index.
Annualized KS-PME; exact rate of out/underperformance vs an index.
Institutional Limited Partners Association; LP best-practice body (not a regulator).
Short-term fund credit facility; can inflate IRR; ILPA limits its use.
The year a fund starts investing; the basis for peer benchmarking.
